medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The College of Medicine partners with other health science schools in the University to offer the Summer Health Professions Education Program (SHPEP).  The SHPEP program targets URM college students interested in pursuing a field within the health professions.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Any student who wishes to request a leave of absence from the College of Medicine must first seek advisement from the Associate Dean for Academic Affairs and the Associate Dean for Student Affairs and Admissions.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Students at the College of Medicine may participate in a wide array of organizations and activities. Participation in these activities promote student initiative, self-expression, cooperation, character development and leadership in the field of medicine. For example students may elect to participate in Student Government, or the Admissions, Recruitment, and Curriculum committees. A wide range of medical interest groups are available -- from the Orthopedic Surgery and Pathology specialty interest groups  to SNMA and Women in Medicine. Students may also volunteer in the New Freedman's Clinic  a once-a-week free clinic for the uninsured.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Rich in cultural, scientific, educational, and business resources, the Washington metropolitan area acts as a stimulus to the intellect, the spirit, the soul. The location of the College of Medicine provides a cosmopolitan setting with a diversity of population and activities.  The campus is Metrorail and Metrobus-accessible and within walking distance of several hospitals. The College of Medicine has a state of the art Clinical Skills Center which provides the ideal environment to teach fundamental and advanced clinical skills.  In addition, the Howard University Health Sciences Simulation Center, which complements the Clinical Skills center, offers students an environment to advance inter-professional education, and to learn basic and advanced  technical skills.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Most medical students live off-campus within a short commute to the university. However there are Howard University affiliated apartments located on-campus.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Howard University is committed to providing an educational, living, and working environment that is welcoming, respectful, and inclusive of all members of the University community, including all sexes, sexual orientations, gender expressions, and gender identities.  There is a student organization with the College of Medicine specifically to support gender and sexual minority students.  The larger university campus also has an Office of Intercultural Affairs and LGBTQ+ Resource Center to support students.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Howard University is committed to ensuring that all students have equal access to the university's programs and offerings.  The Office of Student Accessibility (OSA) provides support to students with disabilities through programming and processing requests for reasonable accommodations ( https://studentaffairs.howard.edu/Accessibility ). The College of Medicine works closely with the OSA to ensure that our applicants and learners with disabilities are provided appropriate accommodations. These support systems may include but are not limited to accommodations related to testing time and test environments.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Each class has a wellness committee that works with Student Affairs in planning wellness programs.  Students have access to Hospital and University wellness programming.  The College of Medicine also sponsors financial wellness workshops for students.  University Counseling Services provide psychological/psychiatric support and the College of Medicine contracts with a psychiatrist specifically for medical students.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The College of Medicine is known for a diverse and inclusive culture.  The learning atmosphere is typically described as a "family" as students/staff/faculty diligently work to support student success academically and future career plans.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Students must make appropriate transportation accommodations to navigate to and from off-site rotations.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Office of Medical Education coordinates academic support programs for all students.  Students are provided individual or group tutoring. Faculty provide support via office hours & review sessions.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students begin to interact with patients during the first semester of the first year of medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Lectures, small group, clinical skills, simulation and team based learning methodologies are employed.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Internal Medicine, Surgery, Obstetrics & Gynecology, Psychiatry, Emergency Medicine, Pediatrics, Neurology, Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation, and Family Medicine.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: For conditional acceptances, there is a 6 week Preliminary Academic Reinforcement Program.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: No, however all small group, team based learning and lab activities are mandatory. Lectures are recorded.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The College of Medicine uses an integrated curriculum.  In the first year, students complete curriculum blocks in Molecules and Cells, Structure and Function, and Population Health. In year two, pathophysiology, pathology and pharmacology are integrated according to organ systems, and the Population Health block is continued. Blocks in Physical Diagnosis and Introduction to Clinical Medicine are also included in year two. The third and fourth years consist of blocks of instruction in a continuum of clerkships and examinations in core clinical disciplines. During the fourth year, opportunity is available for additional clinical or research experience through 24 or 28 weeks of required rotations and  electives. Pedagogical approaches include learning in small group settings, case-based and team-based learning. Students learn and improve  clinical and technical  skills working with standardized patients in our  state-of-the-art Clinical Skills and simulation center.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: The College of Medicine offers and facilitates students' participation in research, at  both intramural and extramural sites. Howard University is a  Research One (R1) Carnegie Classification.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Although not a requirement for graduation, the vast majority of HUCM students are involved in community service through the student council, SNMA and various specialty interest groups.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: While not a requirement, 3/4 of the students complete research prior to graduation, typically during the summer of the first two years.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Affiliated Hospitals include: Howard University Hospital, Children's National Medical Center, Washington V.A. Medical Center and St. Elizabeths.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Honors/Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory, in Year 3, clerkships have an additional designation of HP (High Pass).

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The Howard University College of Medicine is the oldest and largest historically black medical school in the United States and the 36th oldest of all 165 medical schools in this country. The medical college's primary goal at inception remains the college's goal today: to train students to become competent, compassionate physicians who will provide care in medically underserved communities. The college has more than 5,800 living alumni, including approximately 25 percent of all black practicing physicians in this country. Until 1950, the college contributed nearly half of the black physicians in the United States. The 220-bed Howard University Hospital was completed in 1975. It is the college's primary teaching hospital for medical students and is used for postgraduate training in the various specialties of medicine. Medical students also may serve clerkships at the Children's National Medical Center, St. Elizabeth's Hospital and the Washington Veterans Affairs Hospital.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: Howard University College of Medicine provides students of high academic potential with a medical education of exceptional quality and prepares physicians and other health care professionals to serve the underserved. Particular focus is on the education of disadvantaged students for careers in medicine. Special attention is directed to teaching and research activities that address health care disparities.
medSchoolInformation.programUndergradCollege: Howard University, College of Arts & Sciences
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: The BS/MD Program allows the student to complete the requirements for both the B.S. and M.D. degree in six years instead of the customary eight years. A limited number of students enrolled in the College of Arts and Sciences will be admitted each year to the Howard University College of Medicine as part of the entering class of traditionally selected students.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: 14 days, until April 15, 2027 after which it is 5 days or less to respond.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: At a minimum, 2 letters of recommendation from science instructors OR 1 committee letter is required.  A research letter (from Primary Investigator) may substitute for 1 science LOR provided the applicant completed a minimum of 1 full semester research with that investigator.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Interviews are typically held on Tuesdays and Wednesdays from September through April, from 8:30am to 2:30pm.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: One-on-one interviews with admissions committee members.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: The HUCM plans to conduct virtual interviews for 26-27, however this could change.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: While we do not have a residency requirement, transfer students are only considered from LCME accredited medical schools.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: There are no restrictions on out of state applicants.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: We accept a limited number of Canadian applicants.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: We accept a limited number of International applicants.  Scholarships are not available in first year.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: We evaluate DACA applicants on a limited basis.
medSchoolApplication.transferContact: David A. Rose, M.D., Associate Dean Student Affairs and Admissions

**Response to COVID-19, Information for 2027 Admissions Cycle**

Howard University College of Medicine recognizes that the COVID-19 pandemic may have affected your preparation for the medical school application process.  To be flexible, the following adaptations have been made: 

Pass/Fail Grades: We will accept P/F grades for courses taken during the COVID-19 pandemic. A grade of “pass” is required for the course to be accepted. 

Online Courses: We will accept online course work taken at a regionally accredited institution, including labs taken during the pandemic (2020-21).

Activities/Experiences: We recognize that some opportunities have been affected by the pandemic.  A question addressing experiences has been added to our Secondary Application for students to provide an explanation regarding the impact of COVID-19 on their experiences/exposure, if applicable.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: While the committee reviews all MCAT scores, they strongly consider the most recent MCAT.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: An MCAT of 497 is a minimum requirement for screening and granting an interview, exceptions are not made for scores below 497.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: The College of Medicine will accept regionally accredited community college course credits.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Letters will be added to the applicant's file, however the primary focus of the admissions committee will be the content of the primary and secondary application.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: A physician must have the knowledge and skills to function effectively in a broad variety of laboratory and clinical situations. Students matriculating in and graduating from Howard University College of Medicine (COM) must be able to meet the technical requirements of the academic program and not pose a threat to the well-being of patients or themselves. The COM faculty has declared that matriculating students and candidates for admission should have the capabilities and skills described below in order to graduate. The COM requires compliance with these technical standards with or without accommodation.  Please use link below for the full technical standards.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Nearly all of the students enrolled in the College of Medicine receive some sort of financial assistance. Financial aid applicants must submit the FAFSA. Students with demonstrated need may receive school-based scholarships and loans, and those who qualify are recommended for federally guaranteed and private educational loans. Some merit awards are offered to outstanding entering first-year students and for exceptional academic performance in the medical curriculum. Some students receive scholarships funded by the National Health Service Corps, Veterans Affairs or by the military.

medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: No specific date, however, applicants who finished prerequisites greater than 3 years prior, the Admissions Committee looks favorably upon recent (1 year) science coursework completion.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: HUCM conducts a holistic review of applicants' files, some of the pertinent characteristics include but are not limited to the following : (1) character and discernible motivation for a career in medicine, (2) academic record, (3) results of the MCAT (4) letters of recommendation from preprofessional advisors and faculty (5) Health exposure experiences and (6) alignment with mission. Candidates for admission and alternates are selected from among those applicants who satisfy the criteria and who are most likely to serve in underserved communities needing physician services. An invitation for an interview may be extended to an applicant after the Committee on Admissions has made a preliminary examination of the applicant's credentials and has decided that an interview is desirable. There are no residency restrictions. All applicants will be evaluated regardless of the applicants gender, gender identity, race, religion, national or ethnic origin, age, and/or marital status.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: The committee expects that the applicant will have engaged in experiences that places them in health care settings which exposes them to health care professionals interacting with patients and ancillary staff.
